mainTopic: Why מעשר בהמה is not separated nowadays, why מוקדשין are exempt, which animals may be tithed together, and the source that תרומה cannot be separated across kinds
overview: The amud opens by explaining why we still deal with a בכור nowadays but no longer separate מעשר בהמה. With a בכור, following רב יהודה, the owner may put a מום on it before it is born, so no unblemished holy animal exists to be misused. That fix does not work for מעשר. You cannot know which animal will come out tenth. You may not arrange the order, because of לא יבקר. Blemishing the whole herd would also leave no fit animals for קרבנות when the בית המקדש is rebuilt, and even buying animals would not help, since everyone would blemish their herds. Next, the גמרא explains the משנה's rule that מוקדשין are not tithed. It refers to קדשים קלים, which רבי יוסי הגלילי holds belong to the owner, and the פסוק יהיה קדש excludes any animal that is already holy. The גמרא then shows why this needed to be taught: without it, the strict rules of מעשר (no redeeming, no selling) might have applied. Then it shows why sheep and goats are tithed together (the word צאן) while animals from different years are not: a היקש to מעשר דגן, which רבא limits to the year using שנה שנה. Finally, it brings the source that תרומה may not be separated from one kind of produce for another: 'give the best (חלב) of this, and the best of that.'

steps.title: With a firstborn, the problem can be avoided by רב יהודה's method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why בכור is treated differently from מעשר nowadays: there is a practical way around the risk, following רב יהודה, who lets you put a מום on a בכור before it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible to manage, following רב יהודה. רב יהודה said: a person is allowed to put a blemish on a firstborn animal before it comes out into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question on the previous amud: why do we not worry about a תקלה with a בכור the way we do with מעשר? The answer is that with a בכור there is an easy fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on putting a מום on a בכור only applies once it has come out into the world. So while it is still in the womb, the owner may blemish it, and it is born already blemished. A blemished animal cannot be a קרבן, so there is no unblemished holy animal to misuse.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible; there is a workable way
To put a blemish on an animal
A firstborn animal, holy from birth
Into the air of the world, meaning at birth

steps.confusionAlert: Putting a מום on a בכור after it is born is forbidden. רב יהודה only allows it before birth, before it comes out into the air of the world, when the ban on blemishing does not yet apply.

phrases.english: It is possible, following Rav Yehuda,
for Rav Yehuda said:
It is permitted for a person
to put a blemish on a firstborn
before it has come out into the air of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the previous amud about why the בכור is still practiced nowadays.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical workaround that removes the risk
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכור should face the same תקלה concern as מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a בכור, a pre-birth מום prevents the problem.

steps.title: Then do the same for the tithe animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if a מום can be put on an animal in advance, why not do the same for מעשר בהמה and avoid the problem there too?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, with מעשר, one could put a blemish on the animal from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around. If the trick works for a בכור, it should work for מעשר too, so why stop separating מעשר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack uses the בכור logic against the rule about מעשר. If blemishing the animal before it becomes holy removes the risk, the reason for not practicing מעשר seems to fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same applies in this case
That he throws, meaning puts, a blemish on it
From the start, before it becomes holy

phrases.english: Here too,
it is possible to put a blemish on it from the start!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, אֶפְשָׁר דְּשָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer from step 1 to מעשר in order to challenge the rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that מעשר בהמה is not practiced nowadays
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same pre-blemish fix should remove the תקלה concern for מעשר as well.

steps.title: No one knows which animal will be tenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: with מעשר you cannot know in advance which animal will come out tenth, so you do not know which one to blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who knows which one will come out tenth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The fix does not work for מעשר because you do not know beforehand which animal will become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is easy to identify, since it is the first to come out of its mother. With מעשר, the animals pass one by one and whichever is tenth becomes holy. You cannot target a specific animal ahead of time.

keyTerms.meaning: Who knows?
Which one will come out

phrases.english: Who knows which one will come out (as tenth)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (identifiable versus unknown animal)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pre-blemish fix works equally for מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: With מעשר it is impossible to know which animal to blemish.

steps.title: You may not arrange which animal comes out tenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea of placing the blemished animal in the tenth spot on purpose, because the תורה says לא יבקר בין טוב לרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say he should bring out the blemished animal at the head of the tenth spot, the Merciful One said: 'He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a suggested way around the last answer and rejects it. You cannot set up the order so that the blemished animal lands in the tenth spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is to control the line so the pre-blemished animal comes out tenth. The פסוק of לא יבקר forbids choosing or arranging which animal becomes מעשר. The tenth must come out naturally.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; introduces a suggestion the גמרא will reject
At the head of ten, meaning in the tenth spot
He shall not inquire or select (ויקרא כז:לג)
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ as the author of the תורה

phrases.english: And if you will say
that he brings it out at the head of the ten (as the tenth),
'He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad'
the Merciful One said.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ בְּרֵישׁ עַשְׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a possible gap in the answer of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion to control which animal is tenth
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תורה forbids selecting the animal for מעשר (לא יבקר).

steps.title: Blemishing the whole herd would leave nothing for the rebuilt Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects blemishing every animal in the herd, because the בית המקדש may be rebuilt soon and there would be no unblemished animals for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say he could put a blemish on his entire herd: the בית המקדש may soon be rebuilt, and we will need animals to offer, and there will be none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up one more way around the problem and rejects it. Blemishing every animal would guarantee the tenth is blemished, but it would cause a different problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole herd is blemished, no animal could be offered once the בית המקדש is rebuilt. We expect that rebuilding at any moment, so we should not ruin the supply of fit animals. This option therefore fails as well.

keyTerms.meaning: On his whole herd
The בית המקדש will soon be rebuilt
For offering as a קרבן
And there will be none

steps.whatToRemember: All three ways of fixing מעשר fail. You cannot know which animal is tenth. You may not arrange the order (לא יבקר). Blemishing the whole herd ruins the supply for the coming בית המקדש. So מעשר is simply not practiced nowadays.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
it is possible to put a blemish
on his entire herd,
soon the Temple will be rebuilt,
and we will need animals for offering,
and there will be none.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אֶפְשָׁר דְּשָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ עֶדְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a second way around the answer of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion to blemish the entire herd
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would leave no animals fit for קרבנות when the בית המקדש is rebuilt.

steps.title: The same worry should apply to blemishing a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the בכור fix from step 1 with the reasoning of step 5: blemishing firstborns should also leave no animals for the rebuilt בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too with a firstborn animal: the בית המקדש may soon be rebuilt, and we will need animals to offer, and there will be none!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the 'Temple soon rebuilt' argument back onto the בכור. If that worry blocks blemishing for מעשר, it should block blemishing a בכור too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attacks the fix from step 1, the one based on רב יהודה. If people blemish every בכור, those animals will also be unfit for the coming בית המקדש. So the בכור seems to have the same problem.

keyTerms.meaning: So too; the same reasoning applies
With a firstborn animal

phrases.english: So too with a firstborn animal,
soon the Temple will be rebuilt,
and we will need animals for offering,
and there will be none!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 5 to attack the answer of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pre-birth blemish fix for the בכור (step 1)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'Temple soon rebuilt' worry should rule out blemishing firstborns too.

steps.title: Ordinary animals will still be available
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: for a בכור this is no problem, because ordinary non-firstborn animals (פשוטין) will remain unblemished for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible with ordinary animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: blemishing firstborns does not empty the herd of fit animals. The next step uses this same kind of answer to push back on the מעשר side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the firstborns get blemished, and most of the herd is not firstborn. Those ordinary animals stay fit for the rebuilt בית המקדש. Blemishing a whole herd for מעשר leaves nothing, so the בכור fix works while the מעשר fix does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary animals, not firstborns

steps.whatToRemember: The difference between the two cases: a בכור can be blemished before birth, and the herd stays usable thanks to the פשוטין. The next steps test whether something similar (purchased animals) could save the מעשר case.

phrases.english: It is possible with ordinary (non-firstborn) animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (part of the herd versus all of it)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blemishing firstborns would leave no animals for the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Non-firstborn animals remain available, so the בכור fix stands.

steps.title: Why not just buy animals for the rebuilt Temple?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the fear from step 5. Even if everyone blemishes their own herd, purchased animals could still be brought as קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is possible to use purchased animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the worry that blemishing the whole herd would leave nothing for the בית המקדש. It points out that people could simply buy unblemished animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, the בכור problem was solved because ordinary animals stay unblemished. Here the גמרא suggests a similar fix for מעשר: purchased animals (לקוחין) are exempt from מעשר, so nobody needs to blemish them. Those animals would then be available for קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Purchased animals, which are exempt from מעשר בהמה
Here too, applying a similar solution to this case
It is possible, meaning there is a workaround

phrases.english: Here too, it is possible with purchased animals!
phrases.notes: Purchased animals are exempt from מעשר, as the משנה on 55b teaches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of fix used for בכור in step 7 to the מעשר case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that blemishing the whole herd would leave no animals for קרבנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Purchased animals are exempt from מעשר and would stay unblemished, so they could be used for קרבנות.

steps.title: Unblemished animals would become too rare
steps.stepSummary: Everyone would blemish their whole herd, and even tiny blemishes disqualify an animal. So unblemished animals would hardly be found, not even for purchase.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since each owner puts a blemish on his entire herd, and blemishes that disqualify an animal for קדשים are common (even a small mark on the eyelid disqualifies it), unblemished animals would not be commonly found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that buying will not help. Unblemished animals would almost disappear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every animal owner would blemish his own herd, so very few unblemished animals would be left to sell. On top of that, even a tiny blemish, such as one on the eyelid, makes an animal unfit for the מזבח. Together these mean that fit animals would be rare, so the גזירה against separating מעשר nowadays stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts a blemish on an animal
His herd
The eyelid, or a small mark on the eye
Are common or frequently found

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים stopped מעשר בהמה nowadays. Otherwise people would blemish all their animals, and the rebuilt בית המקדש would have almost no fit animals.

phrases.english: Since he puts a blemish on it
phrases.notes: Each owner does this to avoid מעשר.

phrases.english: on his entire herd,
and blemishes that disqualify for sacrifices are common,
for even a mark on the eyelid also disqualifies,
unblemished animals will not be common.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיהוּ שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ עֶדְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: the suggested fix would not actually work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Purchased animals would easily supply the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone blemishes his own herd and blemishes disqualify easily, so fit animals would be scarce even for purchase.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to exclude מוקדשין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that מעשר applies to חולין and not to מוקדשין. It asks why this needs saying, since holy animals do not belong to the owner anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: to non-sacred animals, but not to sacred animals. Sacred animals? That is obvious, they are not his!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, quotes it, and asks why the משנה needed to say something so obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an animal is מוקדש, it belongs to the הקדש and not to its owner. A person cannot make holy something that is not his. So excluding מוקדשין from מעשר seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-sacred animals
Animals dedicated as holy
It is obvious, so why say it?
They are not his

phrases.english: With non-sacred animals but not with sacred animals.
Sacred animals: that is obvious,
they are not his!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words אבל לא במוקדשין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holy animals do not belong to the owner, so it is obvious he cannot separate מעשר from them. The משנה's statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה means קדשים קלים, following רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about קדשים קלים. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, these are still the owner's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to offerings of lesser holiness, and follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said: offerings of lesser holiness are the property of their owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not obvious. It is talking about a type of קרבן that still belongs to its owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשים קלים, such as a שלמים, are considered the owner's money according to רבי יוסי הגלילי. So the reasoning "they are not his" does not apply to them. That makes it a real question whether they could be tithed.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness, such as שלמים
Property of the owners
According to the opinion of

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean קדשים קלים stop being holy. They are fully קדשים. רבי יוסי הגלילי only holds that the owner still has a property stake in them.

phrases.english: With offerings of lesser holiness,
and according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said:
offerings of lesser holiness are the owners' property.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by narrowing the case the משנה is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case and tying it to a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מוקדשין never belong to the owner, so the משנה is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about קדשים קלים, which belong to the owner according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: The ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי says this
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from ומעלה מעל בה׳ that קדשים קלים are the owner's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: "And he commits a trespass against ה׳" comes to include offerings of lesser holiness, which are the owners' property. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that רבי יוסי הגלילי really holds that קדשים קלים belong to the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about someone who swears falsely to deny holding another person's money. רבי יוסי הגלילי includes קדשים קלים in this law. That only makes sense if they count as the owner's money.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
"And he commits a trespass against ה׳‎" (ויקרא ה:כא)
To include

phrases.english: As it was taught: "And he commits a trespass against ה׳"
comes to include offerings of lesser holiness
which are the owners' property,
these are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the opinion that step 11 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי הגלילי holds קדשים קלים are the owner's money
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on the פסוק ומעלה מעל בה׳

steps.title: So the משנה is teaching something new
steps.stepSummary: Since קדשים קלים are the owner's, one might have thought he must tithe them. The משנה teaches that he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought they should be tithed. The משנה comes to teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer: the משנה's rule is not obvious, because there was a real reason to think these animals need מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because these animals are the owner's property, a person could think they fall under the מעשר obligation. The משנה rules out that thought. That explains why it needed to write אבל לא במוקדשין.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say, introducing a mistaken first thought
They should be tithed
It teaches us something new

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say they should be tithed,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא לִיעַשְּׂרוּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 11, now that step 12 has backed it up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the mistaken first thought that the משנה rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קדשים קלים are the owner's property, so they should be tithed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that they are exempt from מעשר.

steps.title: Maybe קדשים קלים really should be tithed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we should not accept that first thought and say that קדשים קלים are tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's exemption. If the logic points toward tithing, maybe they should be tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 called it a mistake to think קדשים קלים need מעשר. The גמרא asks what is actually wrong with that thought, since the owner does own them. It wants a source for the exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is indeed so

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exemption stated in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's exemption of קדשים קלים from מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they are the owner's property, the reasoning supports tithing them, so why reject it?

steps.title: יהיה קדש: only something not yet holy can become מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the tenth "shall be holy," which means it becomes holy now. An animal that is already holy is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says "shall be holy," and not something that is already holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק: מעשר only applies to an animal that is not yet holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words יהיה קדש describe an animal that will become holy through being the tenth. A קדשים קלים animal is already holy, so it cannot "become" holy as מעשר. This exclusion works even though the owner owns the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: "Shall be holy" (ויקרא כז:לב)
The Torah (literally, the Merciful One) said
That is already holy

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר בהמה does not apply to מוקדשין, not even קדשים קלים that belong to the owner. The reason is the פסוק יהיה קדש: only an animal that is not yet holy can become מעשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: The exemption does not depend only on ownership. It is a rule built into what מעשר is: it makes ordinary animals holy, not animals that are already holy.

phrases.english: "Shall be holy," said the Torah,
and not something that is already holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא שֶׁכְּבָר קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning the rule from the wording of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the owner owns קדשים קלים, they should be tithed.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהיה קדש excludes animals that are already holy, so קדשים קלים are exempt.

steps.title: Why would we need a פסוק for this at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 15. If a stringent holiness cannot take effect on an animal with a light holiness, then a light holiness like מעשר surely cannot either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that the Torah wrote "shall be holy." That implies that without this פסוק I would have thought מעשר holiness does take effect on קדשים קלים. But a stringent holiness does not take effect on a light holiness. So is it even necessary to say that a light holiness does not take effect on a light holiness?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 15. It argues that the rule should be obvious even without the פסוק "יהיה קדש".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said we need the פסוק to exclude קדשים קלים from מעשר. The גמרא argues with a קל וחומר: if even a strong holiness cannot take effect on a light one, then the weaker holiness of מעשר certainly cannot. If so, both the פסוק and the משנה seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Merciful One", meaning the Torah or ה׳
I would have thought (an initial assumption)
takes effect, lands on
a stringent, higher level of holiness
a light, lower level of holiness
is it necessary to say? (it is obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: Note that מעשר בהמה itself counts as a light holiness (קדשים קלים). So the question here is about a light holiness landing on an animal that already has a light holiness.

phrases.english: The reason is that the Merciful One wrote "shall be holy,"
which implies that if not for this,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא חָיְילָא קְדוּשַּׁת מַעֲשֵׂר עִילָּוַיְהוּ?
phrases.english: I would have said the holiness of tithe takes effect on them?
Now, if a stringent holiness
does not take effect on a light holiness,
is it necessary to say that a light holiness does not take effect on a light holiness?!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא, הָא לָאו הָכִי הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the פסוק cited in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק "יהיה קדש" is needed to exclude קדשים קלים from מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if a stringent holiness cannot take effect on a light holiness, then a light holiness certainly cannot. The exclusion is therefore obvious.

steps.title: What is the source for that rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a stringent holiness does not take effect on a light one.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask for the source of the rule it just relied on. This is a setup line, and the next step brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 16 depends on the rule that a stronger holiness cannot take effect on a lighter one. Before going further, the גמרא wants to point to where that rule is stated.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for the source)

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the premise used in the קשיא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the rule that a stringent holiness does not take effect on a light holiness

steps.title: The משנה in תמורה: holiness cannot be switched
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that consecrated items cannot be switched from one type of holiness to another. They can only have their value consecrated or dedicated as חרם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Both things consecrated for the altar and things consecrated for Temple upkeep cannot be changed from one holiness to another holiness. But one can consecrate their value (הקדש עילוי), and one can dedicate them as חרם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת תמורה. It shows that once something has one kind of holiness, a different holiness cannot take over, even a more stringent one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For example, an animal that is already a קרבן of light holiness cannot be turned into a more stringent קרבן such as an עולה. What one can do is pledge its value to the Temple treasury, or dedicate that value as חרם. This proves the premise of Step 16, so the קשיא stands strong.

keyTerms.meaning: items consecrated for the altar (קרבנות)
items consecrated for upkeep of the Temple
one may not change or switch
consecrating the monetary value of something
one may dedicate it as חרם (given to the כהנים)

steps.confusionAlert: Consecrating the value (הקדש עילוי) does not change the animal's own holiness. It only obligates the owner to give its value to the Temple.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Both items consecrated for the altar
and items consecrated for Temple maintenance,
one may not change them from one holiness to another holiness,
but one may consecrate them with a consecration of their value,
and one may dedicate them as cherem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by citing the source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה in תמורה: holiness cannot be switched from one type to another, even to a stronger one

steps.title: מעשר is different because every animal is ready for it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought מעשר is different. Every animal is born ready to become מעשר, so an earlier consecration might not cancel its מעשר status.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there, not every animal stands ready to become an עולה. But here, every animal stands ready to become מעשר. So even though he consecrated it as a קרבן, the מעשר status is not removed from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the rule from תמורה is not enough. Someone could have thought that מעשר works differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה in תמורה, the new holiness (like עולה) has no prior claim on the animal, so it cannot push in. מעשר is different: every animal is born with a built-in connection to מעשר. We might have thought that this connection survives even after the animal was made a קרבן קל. That is why the פסוק and the משנה are needed to teach otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (introducing a mistaken initial thought)
stands ready for, is destined for
does not fall away, is not cancelled
the status and prohibitions of מעשר

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a status an object has from birth could have been treated as stronger than a status added to it later. The משנה rejects that idea for מעשר.

phrases.english: You might have said: there,
since not every animal stands to become a burnt offering,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּכׇל בְּהֵמָה לְמַעֲשֵׂר קָיְימָא,
phrases.english: but here, where every animal stands to become tithe,
even though he consecrated it,
the prohibition of tithe is not removed from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16 by distinguishing מעשר from the case in the משנה in תמורה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since every animal is destined for מעשר, its מעשר status might survive even after it was consecrated as a קרבן קל
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק "יהיה קדש" teaches that it does not. An animal that is already holy is not tithed.

steps.title: What practical difference would it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it would make if the מעשר status did stay on an animal that is already a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical result of the הוה אמינא from Step 19. This is a setup line, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is a קרבן קל either way and will be brought on the altar. So the גמרא asks what would change in practice if it also carried מעשר status.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference results from this?

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the הוה אמינא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference if מעשר status remained on an animal that is already a קרבן קל

steps.title: The difference: no redeeming and no selling
steps.stepSummary: If the animal had מעשר status, it could never be redeemed or sold. The משנה teaches that this status does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is regarding the prohibitions of "it shall not be redeemed" and "it shall not be sold." The משנה comes to teach us that these do not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical difference. מעשר may never be redeemed or sold, so the משנה teaches that a קרבן קל does not take on these extra prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים that develops a blemish can be redeemed, but מעשר can never be redeemed or sold. Had the מעשר status stuck, these stricter rules would apply to the animal. The משנה, based on "יהיה קדש", teaches that they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: "It shall not be redeemed", the prohibition on redeeming מעשר
"It shall not be sold", the prohibition on selling מעשר
it teaches us (the new point being made)

steps.whatToRemember: קדשים קלים are not tithed as מעשר בהמה. Without the פסוק we might have thought that מעשר, which applies to every animal from birth, still lands on them. Then the animal could never be redeemed or sold. The משנה teaches that this is not so.

phrases.english: Regarding "it shall not be redeemed" and "it shall not be sold";
so the mishna teaches us that the tithe status does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ וּבְ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 and completes the answer to the קשיא of Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If מעשר status applied, the animal could not be redeemed or sold. The משנה teaches that it does not apply.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The teaching that קדשים קלים are not tithed is needed. It prevents the stricter rules of מעשר (no redeeming, no selling) from applying to them.

steps.title: The משנה: herd and flock are tithed separately, but sheep and goats together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. מעשר בהמה applies to cattle and to sheep and goats. Cattle and sheep are not tithed for each other, but sheep and goats are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The animal tithe applies to cattle and to the flock, but they are not tithed one for the other. It applies to sheep and goats (and they are tithed together), etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה about which animals may be counted together for מעשר בהמה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cattle and flock animals are separate groups, so you cannot count nine cows and one sheep together and give the sheep as מעשר. Sheep and goats, however, both count as one group. The rest of the sugya works out where this rule comes from and how far it goes.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth newborn animal is made holy
Cattle (the herd)
The flock: sheep and goats
Tithed one for the other, meaning counted together as one group

phrases.english: And it applies to cattle and to the flock,
but they are not tithed one for the other;
with sheep and with goats, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: sheep and goats are tithed one for the other; and new and old animals (חדש וישן) are each tithed, but not one for the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section of the משנה. It is not connected to the earlier discussion about holiness taking effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cattle and flock animals are tithed separately. Sheep and goats are tithed together.

steps.title: A logical argument that new and old animals should be tithed together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proposes a קל וחומר. Sheep and goats are different species, yet they are tithed together. Animals born in a new year and an old year are the same species, so they should certainly be tithed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let new and old animals be tithed for each other, by a קל וחומר. Sheep and goats are כלאים with each other, and yet they are tithed one for the other. New and old animals are not כלאים with each other, so isn't it logical that they should be tithed one for the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a logical argument that would allow animals from different years to be counted together. This sets up the verse that will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sheep and goats are different enough to count as כלאים, yet they still join for מעשר. The argument says the bar for joining must be low, so new and old animals, which are the same species, should easily join. This argument is about to be blocked by a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
Forbidden mixtures, here meaning different species that may not be bred together
New and old, meaning animals born in the current year and in the previous year
Is it not logical? (the closing formula of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final הלכה. It is a suggested argument (הוה אמינא) that the ברייתא brings only so that it can reject it.

phrases.english: And let new and old
be tithed one for the other
by an a fortiori argument:
If sheep and goats,
which are diverse kinds with each other,
are tithed one for the other,
then new and old,
which are not diverse kinds with each other,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיִּתְעַשְּׂרוּ מִזֶּה עַל זֶה?
phrases.english: is it not logical that they should be tithed one for the other?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיִהְיוּ חָדָשׁ וְיָשָׁן מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה's rule about sheep and goats to argue for a wider rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that new and old animals are not tithed together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two different species can join, then animals of the same species from different years should certainly be able to join.

steps.title: The verse compares animal tithe to grain tithe, so new and old cannot join
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר using "עשר תעשר". The doubled word teaches two tithes, animal and grain, and links them. Grain is never tithed from new for old, so animals are not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "עשר תעשר". The verse is speaking about two tithes: one is the animal tithe and the other is the grain tithe. It compares the animal tithe to the grain tithe. Just as the grain tithe is not taken from new for old, so too the animal tithe is not taken from new for old.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses a verse to cancel the logical argument. The verse ties animal tithe to grain tithe, and grain tithe never mixes years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse overrides a קל וחומר. The double wording "עשר תעשר" points to two tithes, and the Torah links them with a היקש. Since grain from different years cannot be tithed together, animals born in different years cannot be either.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse says (introduces a verse that settles the question)
"You shall surely tithe" (דברים יד:כב)
The tithe of grain
Compares or links (a היקש: two laws are equated by the verse)

steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש is the source for the rule that animals from different years are tithed separately. The rest of the sugya asks how far this comparison reaches.

phrases.english: The verse states: "You shall tithe a tithe";
the verse is speaking of two tithes,
one is the animal tithe
and one is the grain tithe,
and it compares the animal tithe to the grain tithe:

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן מֵחָדָשׁ עַל הַיָּשָׁן לֹא,
phrases.english: just as grain tithe is not taken from the new for the old,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה מֵחָדָשׁ עַל הַיָּשָׁן לֹא.
phrases.english: so too animal tithe is not taken from the new for the old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 23 using a verse.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A verse links animal tithe to grain tithe, and grain tithe does not allow mixing years. Logic cannot override the verse.

steps.title: Then the comparison should also stop sheep and goats from joining
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the היקש. Grain tithe is never taken from one species for another, so by the same comparison, sheep and goats should not be tithed together either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us also say about sheep and goats: the verse compares animal tithe to grain tithe. Just as grain tithe is not taken from one species for a different species, so too animal tithe should not be taken from one species for a different species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison further and finds a problem. If animal tithe follows grain tithe, then sheep and goats should not be able to join.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היקש should carry over all the rules of grain tithe, not just one. Grain cannot be tithed across species, and sheep and goats are different species. This would contradict the משנה, which says sheep and goats do join.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on the previous answer)
From one species for a different species
Let us say

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כְּבָשִׂים וְעִזִּים נָמֵי לֵימָא:
phrases.english: If so, let us say about sheep and goats too:
the verse compares animal tithe to grain tithe;
just as grain tithe
is not taken from one type for another type,
so too animal tithe
is not taken from one type for another type?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כְּבָשִׂים וְעִזִּים נָמֵי לֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the היקש from step 24 by applying it to a different rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that sheep and goats are tithed together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the היקש transfers grain tithe's rules, it should also transfer the ban on tithing across species.

steps.title: The word צאן includes both sheep and goats
steps.stepSummary: The Torah used the word "צאן", which covers both sheep and goats. This extra inclusion lets them be tithed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One included them with the word "צאן".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a specific word in the Torah includes sheep and goats together, so the היקש does not separate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about מעשר בהמה (ויקרא 27:32) says "צאן", a word that covers both sheep and goats. This direct inclusion is stronger than the general comparison to grain. So on this point animal tithe is an exception to the grain model.

keyTerms.meaning: Included or added (from the word for increasing)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: The Merciful One included them with "flock."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a verse that specifically includes this case and overrides the general comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The היקש to grain should keep sheep and goats apart.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word "צאן" includes sheep and goats together, so they may join.

steps.title: Then צאן should also join new and old animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if "צאן" is an inclusion that overrides the היקש, it should also include new and old animals together.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, new and old should also be tithed together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer back on itself. If "צאן" breaks the comparison to grain, it should break it for new and old animals too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once one inclusion can override the היקש, there seems no reason it should only override one rule. So the rule from step 24 about new and old is now in question.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: If so, new and old too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 24 that new and old are not tithed together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "צאן" overrides the היקש, it should override it for new and old as well.

steps.title: The verse עשר תעשר keeps new and old apart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that "עשר תעשר" is written, and that verse specifically keeps new and old animals apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written "עשר תעשר"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replies that a verse stands behind the new-and-old rule, so "צאן" cannot cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each rule now has its own verse. "צאן" joins sheep and goats, and "עשר תעשר" separates new and old. The next step asks why each verse controls the rule it was given, and step 30 (רבא) answers.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written

phrases.english: But it is written: "You shall tithe a tithe."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to the verse that is the source of the rule being challenged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "צאן" should let new and old join.
steps.terutzMaskana: "עשר תעשר" keeps new and old separate.

steps.title: Why apply the comparison to years but not to species?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason we have to use the היקש for new and old, and use "צאן" for sheep and goats, rather than the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see (to decide this way)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a reason behind the split. Why does each verse control the rule we gave it, and not the opposite?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses are available. In theory one could say "צאן" joins new and old while the היקש separates sheep and goats. The גמרא demands a reason for choosing one way.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? (What reason do you have to choose this way?)

phrases.english: And what did you see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way steps 26 and 28 assign each verse to its rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to apply the היקש to years and the word "צאן" to species.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a reason, the two verses could be assigned the opposite way.

steps.title: רבא: the verse limits the comparison to the matter of the year
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the same verse says "שנה שנה". This shows the היקש to grain is only about the year, not about anything else such as species.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse says "שנה שנה" (year by year). I compared them only regarding the year, and not regarding anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes the discussion by showing that the verse itself limits the comparison to the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "שנה שנה" come right after "עשר תעשר". They show that the link between animal tithe and grain tithe is only about not mixing years. So the היקש separates new and old animals but does not separate species, and "צאן" freely joins sheep and goats.

keyTerms.meaning: "Year by year" (דברים יד:כב)
I compared it (the תורה speaking: I made the היקש)
For another matter

steps.whatToRemember: Sheep and goats are tithed together because the Torah says "צאן". Animals from different years are not tithed together because of the היקש to מעשר דגן. As רבא shows from "שנה שנה", that comparison applies only to the year.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The verse says "year by year";
I compared it regarding the year,
and not regarding another matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29 and closes the sugya.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the היקש using a nearby word in the verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The היקש might apply to every rule of grain tithe, including species.
steps.terutzMaskana: The היקש applies only to years, so new and old are separate while sheep and goats join.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "שנה שנה" limits the היקש to the year. New and old animals are not tithed together, but sheep and goats are.

steps.title: A משנה: no separating תרומה from one kind for another kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת תרומות. It says you may not separate תרומה from one kind of produce to cover a different kind, and if you do, it is not תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: One may not separate תרומה from one kind of produce to cover produce that is not its kind. And if he did separate that way, his תרומה is not תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting a rule from another משנה. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will ask for the source of this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has two parts. First, you should not do it from the start (לכתחילה). Second, even after the fact (בדיעבד), it does not work at all, because the separated portion simply does not become תרומה. That second part is strong, so the גמרא will want a clear source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, in a משנה from a different מסכת
Separating תרומה, the portion of produce given to a כהן
From one kind of produce to cover a different kind
His תרומה does not count as תרומה at all

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'one may not' with 'it does not work.' This משנה says both: you should not do it, and if you do, the separation is completely invalid.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ,
phrases.english: One may not separate teruma from one type for what is not its type,
and if he separated, his teruma is not teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section. It moves from the topic of מעשר בהמה to a related rule about תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה separated from one kind of produce for a different kind is invalid, even after the fact.

steps.title: Where does this rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the rule in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these words (this rule)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule it just quoted. It is not attacking the rule; it only wants to know where it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה says the תרומה is completely invalid, the גמרא wants a verse that shows the Torah requires each kind to be handled separately.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these words? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule from the משנה in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that תרומה cannot be separated from one kind to cover another kind.

steps.title: The source: 'the best of this and the best of that'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי, quoting רבי ינאי (or, some say, ריש לקיש), learns the rule from the verse 'כל חלב יצהר וכל חלב תירוש ודגן.' The Torah says to give 'the best' of each kind separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי ינאי (and some say: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש): The verse says 'All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine and grain.' The Torah is saying: give 'the best' from this one, and 'the best' from that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a verse. The Torah lists 'the best' (חלב) separately for oil and for wine and grain, which shows that each kind needs its own תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is that the word חלב ('the best') is repeated for each kind of produce. That repetition tells us each kind has its own required gift. So תרומה taken from one kind cannot cover a different kind. There is a disagreement only about who said this teaching (רבי ינאי or ריש לקיש), not about the teaching itself.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it this way, giving a different version of who said the teaching
Literally 'fat'; here it means 'the best part,' referring to תרומה
Oil
Wine
Grain

steps.confusionAlert: Here חלב does not mean forbidden animal fat. In this verse it means 'the best portion' of the produce.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule against separating תרומה from one kind for another comes from the repeated word 'חלב' in the verse: give 'the best' of each kind separately.
steps.whyThisMatters: This verse sets up a basic principle: each kind of produce needs its own gift. That principle can then be compared to other gifts, such as tithes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yannai said,
and some say: Rabbi Ami said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
"All the best of the oil
and all the best of the wine and grain" —
the Torah said:
Give the best for this one, and the best for that one.
